_OBJECTIVE: Verify that X-band PSR (9 GHz) shows more Pd reduction than S-band in the SAME rain conditions. Paired with TC-03 (S-band) with symmetric sensor geometry so the ONLY variable is CenterFrequency, which isolates ITU-R P.838-3 attenuation as the test subject.
_PASS_CRITERIA: X-band target detection count <= S-band target detection count at same rain rate. This isolates the frequency-dependent attenuation from rain rate effects.
_NOTE: Both TC-03 and TC-04 use config/weather/rain/validation_rain.json (16 mm/hr, 5-50s storm window aligned to the 50s gentle_turn scenario) and symmetric PSR sensors (sband_PSR / xband_PSR, both 111 km rangeLimits). The ONLY variable between the two tests is CenterFrequency. Previously used default_rain (storm at 50-130s, never fires during scenario) and asymmetric sensors (default_PSR 20 km vs xband_PSR 111 km) -- both were fixed in v3.4.2.
description: TC-04: X-band PSR (9 GHz, symmetric geometry) in moderate rain (16 mm/hr) -- expect notably more degradation than TC-03
